title.value: SmOOD: Smoothness-based Out-of-Distribution Detection Approach for Surrogate Neural Networks in Aircraft Design
title.justification: The paper title accurately reflects its focus on developing a new detection approach (SmOOD) for surrogate neural networks in aircraft design.
title.quote: SmOOD: Smoothness-based Out-of-Distribution Detection Approach for Surrogate Neural Networks in Aircraft Design

extractions.description: The paper introduces SmOOD, a smoothness-based out-of-distribution detection approach for surrogate neural networks, particularly in aircraft design. It addresses the challenges faced by feedforward neural networks in design optimization due to their inability to generalize well to out-of-distribution samples. SmOOD uses the smoothness properties of high-fidelity simulations to detect OODs, ensuring the surrogate model produces reliable predictions. This method is assessed across various aircraft performance models, demonstrating improved predictive performance and computational efficiency compared to Gaussian Process models.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: Although the paper deals with optimization in aircraft design, which can indirectly impact resource efficiency, the central focus is on computational efficiency and model performance in detecting out-of-distribution samples, rather than on climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Aircraft industry is constantly striving for more efficient design optimization methods in terms of human efforts, computation time, and resources consumption.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on computational methods in aircraft design optimization, which does not directly address any specific climate or ecological sustainable development goals.
primary_category.quote: Feedforward neural networks (FNNs) can capture highly nonlinear input-output mappings, yielding efficient surrogates for aircraft performance factors.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper contributes to more efficient resource usage in aircraft design, which could potentially lead to reduced emissions and energy use, aligning with broader climate change mitigation efforts.
secondary_categories.quote: Aircraft industry is constantly striving for more efficient design optimization methods in terms of human efforts, computation time, and resources consumption.

primary_sub_category.justification: The main focus is on developing a computational method for detecting out-of-distribution samples in surrogate models, not directly addressing any specific climate or ecological sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: By using SmOOD, only high-risk OOD inputs are forwarded to the HF model for re-evaluation, leading to more accurate results at a low overhead cost.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: While primarily focusing on aircraft design, improvements in design optimization methods can indirectly influence energy efficiency practices.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Hybrid surrogate optimization maintains high results quality while providing rapid design assessments.

applications.justification: The paper's method, SmOOD, is directly applied to optimize aircraft design processes by improving surrogate model reliability and reducing computational costs.
applications.quote: Hybrid surrogate optimization maintains high results quality while providing rapid design assessments when both the surrogate model and the switch mechanism for eventually transitioning to the HF model are calibrated properly.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories and sub-categories sufficiently capture any indirect links the paper may have with sustainability; thus, no new category is required.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The existing sub-categories already encompass the paper's remote connections to sustainability through resource efficiency in computational methods; no new sub-category is needed.
